rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-5 report the authors' own field measurements (flow meters and pressure sensors at the upstream end and four hydrants of the Lucefecit network, 2000-2002) and their own ICARE/AKLA simulation runs calibrated against observed head losses (Fig. 6).
rows.notes: The study is a primary hydraulic performance analysis of one on-demand pressurized network (Lucefecit, Portugal). It reports nothing on investment cost of on-demand networks, nor on cost being driven by guaranteeing supply at peak. Its own results concern hydraulic performance during the peak period: with the design upstream piezometric elevation (260 m) fewer than 10% of hydrant configurations are satisfied at the recorded peak discharge, and even after raising Zo to 265 m three hydrants still show large relative pressure deficits and low reliability (Figs. 7-11). If anything it shows that supply at peak was not fully guaranteed in this system. It also notes observed peak discharges (737 and 656 l/s) were well below the design discharge (1153 l/s). No evidence on the claimed cost effect, so Q2 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study addresses hydraulic performance (pressure deficit, reliability) of an on-demand network, not investment cost; the review's citation for the cost claim is not supported by any result in this paper.
